## §2d — 3'UTR / CDS sanity at n=130

Three additional structural features for the same `sec_A_groups`: CDS length,
translation-based 3'UTR (`tx_len − own_stop_tx_pos`), and bias-corrected
3'UTR via the `utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt` field of `ref_atg` (walks past PTCs
to find the next non-PTC stop). The non-PTC measure is the more meaningful
3'UTR-length comparator because for PTC+ pairs the translation-based 3'UTR
inflates with PTC distance and is no longer comparable to the Control 3'UTR.

```{r sec2d-features, include=FALSE}
own_atg_tx_lookup <- (function() {
  atg_tx <- rep(NA_integer_, nrow(coding_cds))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(coding_cds))) {
    si <- struct_idx[i]; if (is.na(si)) next
    strand <- coding_cds$strand[i]
    if (is.na(strand) || strand == "") next
    atg_g <- if (strand == "+") coding_cds$cds_start[i] else coding_cds$cds_stop[i]
    atg_tx[i] <- Isopair::genomicToTranscript(
      atg_g, structures$exon_starts[[si]], structures$exon_ends[[si]], strand)
  }
  setNames(atg_tx, coding_cds$isoform_id)
})()

tx_len_lookup <- setNames(
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(structures)), function(i)
    sum(structures$exon_ends[[i]] - structures$exon_starts[[i]] + 1L),
    integer(1)),
  structures$isoform_id
)

# Build per-comparator features for sec_A_groups
ra_c2_lookup <- setNames(
  as.data.table(ref_atg$c2)$utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt,
  as.data.table(ref_atg$c2)$comparator_isoform_id
)
ra_c4_lookup <- setNames(
  as.data.table(ref_atg$c4)$utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt,
  as.data.table(ref_atg$c4)$comparator_isoform_id
)

compute_secA_feat <- function(comp_ids, ra_lookup) {
  own_stop <- own_stop_tx_lookup$own_stop_tx_pos[match(comp_ids, own_stop_tx_lookup$isoform_id)]
  own_atg  <- own_atg_tx_lookup[comp_ids]
  tx_len   <- tx_len_lookup[comp_ids]
  data.table(
    comparator_isoform_id = comp_ids,
    cds_nt   = pmax(0L, own_stop - own_atg + 1L),
    utr3_nt  = pmax(0L, tx_len - own_stop),
    utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt = ra_lookup[comp_ids]
  )
}

feat_ptc_pos <- compute_secA_feat(ptc_pos_ids, ra_c2_lookup)
feat_ptc_neg <- compute_secA_feat(ptc_neg_ids, ra_c2_lookup)
feat_ctrl    <- compute_secA_feat(gencode_all3_c4$comparator_isoform_id, ra_c4_lookup)
# At the n=130 all-3-ENST + coding-CDS scope every comparator's own GENCODE
# stop is non-PTC by classification (PTC+ pairs were segregated via §2a's
# has_ptc flag), so for PTC- and Control the bias-corrected 3'UTR length IS
# the translation-based measure. Overwrite unconditionally (matches the
# figure-side CDSand3UTR_GENCODEonly/data_export.R convention).
feat_ptc_neg[, utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt := utr3_nt]
feat_ctrl[,    utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt := utr3_nt]

cds_lookup <- setNames(
  c(feat_ptc_pos$cds_nt, feat_ptc_neg$cds_nt, feat_ctrl$cds_nt),
  c(feat_ptc_pos$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ptc_neg$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ctrl$comparator_isoform_id)
)
utr3_lookup <- setNames(
  c(feat_ptc_pos$utr3_nt, feat_ptc_neg$utr3_nt, feat_ctrl$utr3_nt),
  c(feat_ptc_pos$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ptc_neg$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ctrl$comparator_isoform_id)
)
utr3_npstop_lookup <- setNames(
  c(feat_ptc_pos$utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt,
    feat_ptc_neg$utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt,
    feat_ctrl$utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt),
  c(feat_ptc_pos$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ptc_neg$comparator_isoform_id,
    feat_ctrl$comparator_isoform_id)
)

secA_cds_desc  <- group_descriptives(sec_A_groups, cds_lookup,
                                      c("NMD+/PTC+", "NMD+/PTC-", "Control"))
secA_cds_pw    <- pairwise_stats(sec_A_groups, cds_lookup)
secA_utr3_desc <- group_descriptives(sec_A_groups, utr3_lookup,
                                      c("NMD+/PTC+", "NMD+/PTC-", "Control"))
secA_utr3_pw   <- pairwise_stats(sec_A_groups, utr3_lookup)
secA_utr3np_desc <- group_descriptives(sec_A_groups, utr3_npstop_lookup,
                                        c("NMD+/PTC+", "NMD+/PTC-", "Control"))
secA_utr3np_pw   <- pairwise_stats(sec_A_groups, utr3_npstop_lookup)

secA_cds_pw$wilcox_p_fmt    <- vapply(secA_cds_pw$wilcox_p,    format_p, character(1))
secA_utr3_pw$wilcox_p_fmt   <- vapply(secA_utr3_pw$wilcox_p,   format_p, character(1))
secA_utr3np_pw$wilcox_p_fmt <- vapply(secA_utr3np_pw$wilcox_p, format_p, character(1))
```

### CDS length

```{r sec2d-cds, echo=FALSE}
# Claim 4.6.4's third assertion — "no significant difference in CDS length". A NULL result, so
# what has to be recorded is the p-value of each comparison involving NMD+/PTC-, not a median:
# the claim is that neither reaches significance, and one of the two being null is not the
# claim. Supporting numbers, since the paper prints none.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(secA_cds_pw))) {
  gx <- secA_cds_pw$group_x[i]; gy <- secA_cds_pw$group_y[i]
  if (!("NMD+/PTC-" %in% c(gx, gy))) next
  claim_emit("4.6.4", sprintf("Wilcoxon p for CDS length, %s vs %s", gx, gy),
             secA_cds_pw$wilcox_p[i], n = nrow(secA_cds_desc),
             population = SEC_A_FEATURE_POP)
}

knitr::kable(secA_cds_desc, caption = "CDS length (nt)",

             caption = "CDS length — pairwise stats",
             col.names = c("X","Y","Med X","Med Y","HL shift","HL 95% CI","Cliff's δ","Wilcoxon p"))
```

```{r sec3d-refaug-cds-utr3-export, include=FALSE}
nmd_C <- refaug_matched_c2[, .(comparator_isoform_id, group = group3,
                                cds_nt = comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg,
                                utr3_to_tx_end_nt, utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt)]
ctrl_C <- refaug_matched_c4[, .(comparator_isoform_id, group = "Control",
                                 cds_nt = comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg,
                                 utr3_to_tx_end_nt, utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt)]
all_feat_C <- rbind(nmd_C, ctrl_C, fill = TRUE)
all_feat_C[, group := factor(group, levels = c("NMD+/PTC+", "NMD+/PTC-", "Control"))]

SF33_DATA <- file.path(.nmd_root, "figures/supplemental/SF33_CdsAnd3UTR_GENCODE/data")
dir.create(SF33_DATA, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

data.table::fwrite(
  all_feat_C[, .(comparator_isoform_id, group, cds_nt,
                 utr3_to_tx_end_nt, utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt)],
  file.path(SF33_DATA, "features_1166_subset_long.tsv"), sep = "\t")

emit_per_measure_C <- function(measure_col, slug) {
  groups <- c("NMD+/PTC+", "NMD+/PTC-", "Control")
  desc <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(groups, function(g) {
    vals <- all_feat_C[group == g, get(measure_col)]; vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
    data.table::data.table(group = g, n = length(vals), median = median(vals),
                           q25 = quantile(vals, 0.25), q75 = quantile(vals, 0.75))
  }))
  data.table::fwrite(desc, file.path(SF33_DATA, sprintf("%s_descriptives.tsv", slug)), sep = "\t")
  pairs <- list(c("NMD+/PTC-", "NMD+/PTC+"), c("NMD+/PTC-", "Control"),
                c("NMD+/PTC+", "Control"))
  pw <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    a <- all_feat_C[group == p[1], get(measure_col)]; a <- a[!is.na(a)]
    b <- all_feat_C[group == p[2], get(measure_col)]; b <- b[!is.na(b)]
    w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(a, b, conf.int = TRUE))
    data.table::data.table(
      group_x = p[1], group_y = p[2], n_x = length(a), n_y = length(b),
      median_x = median(a), median_y = median(b),
      hl_shift = as.numeric(w$estimate),
      hl_ci_lo = as.numeric(w$conf.int[1]), hl_ci_hi = as.numeric(w$conf.int[2]),
      cliffs_delta = (sum(outer(a, b, ">")) - sum(outer(a, b, "<"))) / (length(a) * length(b)),
      wilcox_p = w$p.value)
  }))
  data.table::fwrite(pw, file.path(SF33_DATA, sprintf("%s_pairwise.tsv", slug)), sep = "\t")
  invisible(NULL)
}
emit_per_measure_C("cds_nt",                   "panelD_cds_length_refaug")
emit_per_measure_C("utr3_to_tx_end_nt",        "panelE_utr3_translation_refaug")
emit_per_measure_C("utr3_via_non_ptc_stop_nt", "panelF_utr3_non_ptc_stop_refaug")

secC_utr3_desc   <- fread(file.path(SF33_DATA, "panelE_utr3_translation_refaug_descriptives.tsv"))
secC_utr3np_desc <- fread(file.path(SF33_DATA, "panelF_utr3_non_ptc_stop_refaug_descriptives.tsv"))
secC_utr3_pw     <- fread(file.path(SF33_DATA, "panelE_utr3_translation_refaug_pairwise.tsv"))
secC_utr3np_pw   <- fread(file.path(SF33_DATA, "panelF_utr3_non_ptc_stop_refaug_pairwise.tsv"))
```

The bias-correction pattern (PTC+ inflation under translation-based collapses under non-PTC-stop measure) replicates across both scopes.", out.width="100%"}

# §3 — Larger-scope replication at ref-AUG-traceable (n=819)

Section C extends Section A by relaxing the all-3-ENST + coding-CDS
constraints and instead routing through the ref-AUG-projected ORF
classification. This roughly 6× larger cohort lets us check that Section A's
PTC findings replicate at the larger scope without relying on TD2's CDS calls
on novel comparators.

**Scope construction** (replicated from
[`figures/multipanel/figure4_ptcneg_and_model/data_export.R`](../../../../figures/multipanel/figure4_ptcneg_and_model/data_export.R) §"Section C scope"):

     flowchart can label itself from computed values instead of hardcoded literals.
     It is include=FALSE and emits nothing, so nothing moved visibly. 2026-07-26 -->

```

Control pairs. Both arms share the same
`r format(nrow(shared_keys), big.mark=",")` `(gene, reference)` pairs.

**Mechanism classification** of the NMD arm (`mechanism_class_4()` on the

# ── Claim 4.7.4 — PTC+ rate at the reference AUG-traceable scope ──────────────────────

n_secC      <- nrow(refaug_matched_c2)

### Section C CDS / 3'UTR feature export (SF33 / SF36)

Migrated here from `figures/supplemental/SF33_CdsAnd3UTR_GENCODE/data_export.R`
on 2026-07-28 (S13: no result may originate in `figures/`). That script did not
merely export — it **rebuilt the Section C cohort itself**, repeating the
`sec3-scope` construction and the `mechanism_class → group3` classification, so
one population was defined in two places and only one of them could be checked
by re-rendering this report (S4). Claim 4.7.5's operative half — that the 3'UTR
effect is limited to the ref-AUG-traceable set — was produced entirely outside
the report layer.

**Proven output-preserving before the move.** Both constructions were run against
the same tree and compared: the same 833/833 cohort with an identical key set, an
identical 1,666-row feature table, and identical descriptives and pairwise tables
for all three measures. The `n = 1,166` in the old script's header was a stale
legacy-tree vintage, not a different scope.


```{r sec3d-utr3-tables, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(secC_utr3_desc, caption = "Section C 3'UTR length, translation-based (ref-AUG-projected stop → tx end)")
knitr::kable(secC_utr3np_desc, caption = "Section C 3'UTR length, bias-corrected (non-PTC-stop based)")
```

Claim 4.7.5 asserts the 3'UTR effect is *limited to* the ref-AUG-traceable set.
Read against both scopes, that holds under the **bias-corrected** measure and
fails under the **translation-based** one, so the sentence needs its measure named.

```{r sec3d-utr3-4-7-5, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  rbind(secC_utr3_pw[, .(measure = "translation-based", group_x, group_y,
                         median_x, median_y, wilcox_p)],
        secC_utr3np_pw[, .(measure = "bias-corrected", group_x, group_y,
                           median_x, median_y, wilcox_p)]),
  caption = "Section C 3'UTR pairwise tests — the comparison claim 4.7.5 rests on")

# ── Claim 4.7.5 — "limited to the Reference AUG-traceable set only" ────────────────────
# A CONTRAST ACROSS TWO SCOPES, so BOTH have to be emitted or the word "limited" is unchecked:
# the claim fails if the effect is also present in the GENCODE reference set. It is also
# measure-dependent and the sentence names no measure, which is the defect on record -- so both
# the translation-based and the bias-corrected test are emitted, for both scopes, four rows.
# All supporting: the paper prints no number here.
# BASE-R SUBSETTING, DELIBERATELY: Section A's pairwise table is a data.frame (from
# pairwise_stats) and Section C's is a data.table (from fread), so data.table's
# unquoted-column syntax works on one and raises "object 'group_x' not found" on the other.
# Measured -- it halted the knit at this chunk after 56 emissions had already been written.
utr3_p <- function(pw) {
  i <- which(pw$group_x == "NMD+/PTC+" & pw$group_y == "Control")
  if (!length(i)) i <- which(pw$group_x == "Control" & pw$group_y == "NMD+/PTC+")
  if (!length(i)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(pw$wilcox_p[i[1]])
}
MEASURE_DEF <- c(
  "translation-based" = paste("3'UTR measured from the isoform's own stop codon to the",
                              "transcript end, so a PTC inflates it by construction"),
  "bias-corrected"    = paste("3'UTR measured from the first NON-PTC stop codon, walking past",
                              "a PTC, which removes that inflation"))
for (spec in list(
      list(pw = secA_utr3_pw,   scope = "GENCODE reference set",       m = "translation-based",
           pop = SEC_A_POPULATION),
      list(pw = secA_utr3np_pw, scope = "GENCODE reference set",       m = "bias-corrected",
           pop = SEC_A_POPULATION),
      list(pw = secC_utr3_pw,   scope = "reference AUG-traceable set", m = "translation-based",
           pop = SEC_C_POPULATION),
      list(pw = secC_utr3np_pw, scope = "reference AUG-traceable set", m = "bias-corrected",
           pop = SEC_C_POPULATION))) {
  claim_emit("4.7.5",
             sprintf("Wilcoxon p, 3'UTR length PTC+ vs Control, %s measure, %s",
                     spec$m, spec$scope),
             utr3_p(spec$pw),
             population = paste0(spec$pop, ". ", MEASURE_DEF[[spec$m]]))
}
```

## §3a — 5'UTR length + longest 5'UTR ORF at Section C

At the n=819 scope, most NMD comparators are novel (TD2-anchored CDS not
reliable for 5'UTR measurement) — so we use `utr5_features_refaug`, which is
the 5'UTR delimited by the ref-AUG-projected start. Three groups (from §3
classification): NMD+/PTC+, NMD+/PTC− (ORF match + ORF diff merged), Control.

```{r sec3a-secC-groups, include=FALSE}

  "NMD+/PTC+" = refaug_matched_c2[group3 == "NMD+/PTC+", comparator_isoform_id],
  "NMD+/PTC-" = refaug_matched_c2[group3 == "NMD+/PTC-", comparator_isoform_id],

)

secC_orf_desc  <- group_descriptives(sec_C_groups, u5_orf_ra,

secC_orf_pw    <- pairwise_stats(sec_C_groups, u5_orf_ra)
secC_utr5_pw$wilcox_p_fmt <- vapply(secC_utr5_pw$wilcox_p, format_p, character(1))
secC_orf_pw$wilcox_p_fmt  <- vapply(secC_orf_pw$wilcox_p,  format_p, character(1))

## §3b — PTC rate at Section C

Already computed inline in the §3 scope construction:
`r format(sec3_class$n[sec3_class$group == "NMD+/PTC+"], big.mark=",")` PTC+ /
`r format(nrow(refaug_matched_c2), big.mark=",")` =
**`r round(100 * sec3_class$n[sec3_class$group == "NMD+/PTC+"] / nrow(refaug_matched_c2), 1)`%** at this scope (vs 37.9% at the n=130
all-3-ENST scope). The classifier definitions differ —
see §5 for reconciliation.

# §4 — TD2 bias evidence (TD2BiasEvidence supplement)

Scope (broad): `refaug_matched_c2 ∩ TD2 CDS available ∩ ref-AUG ORF computable
∩ ref AUG exonic` → n=819 broad.
Scope (occult-PTC): broad `∩ effectively_ptc ∩ original_ptc == FALSE` → n=348.

**Scope construction.** Broad (n=819) = `refaug_matched_c2` ∩ TD2 CDS
available ∩ ref-AUG ORF computable ∩ ref AUG exonic. Occult-PTC (n=348) =
broad ∩ `category == "effectively_ptc"` ∩ `original_ptc == FALSE` — pairs
where ref-AUG tracing revealed a PTC that TD2 missed. This is the population
in which TD2's PTC-avoidance bias is most pronounced.

```{r sec4-scope, include=FALSE}
c2_full_dt <- as.data.table(refaug_matched_c2)
comp_cds   <- cds[match(c2_full_dt$comparator_isoform_id, isoform_id)]
c2_full_dt[, strand_use      := comp_cds$strand]
c2_full_dt[, td2_atg_genomic := ifelse(comp_cds$strand == "+",
                                       comp_cds$cds_start, comp_cds$cds_stop)]
c2_full_dt[, td2_orf_nt      := comp_cds$orf_length * 3L]
c2_full_dt[, ref_atg_orf_nt  := comp_orf_length_from_ref_atg]

broad <- c2_full_dt[!is.na(td2_orf_nt) & !is.na(ref_atg_orf_nt) &
                     ref_atg_exonic_in_comp == TRUE]
```

`broad` = `r format(nrow(broad), big.mark=",")` pairs (matches the
n=819 TD2BiasEvidence supplement scope).

```{r sec4-compute, include=FALSE}
# CACHING REMOVED 2026-07-30 (Pete's call, W134). This chunk was cache=TRUE with
# cache.extra=tools::md5sum(FASTA_PATH). Three reasons it had to go, in order of severity:
#
# 1. The cache directory was TRACKED IN GIT, so it shipped. .gitignore had no cache rule, and a
#    git add on the directory swept it in at 6332ffd. D1 forecloses intermediate data in the
#    citable repo, and a knitr cache is intermediate data by any reading.
# 2. cache.extra covered ONLY the FASTA. This chunk also reads the isopair intermediates, so the
#    key could not notice them changing -- which is exactly the case a deposit-native rebuild
#    creates. Anyone who did hit the cache would see section 4 "reproduce" regardless of what
#    their own intermediates contained.
# 3. tools::md5sum() returns a PATH-NAMED vector, so the key silently included the deposit's
#    ABSOLUTE PATH. That makes the cache non-portable on principle: it can only ever hit on the
#    machine that wrote it, so it could never do its job in a repo meant for readers.
#
# The saving was never measured. The whole report renders in 42 s uncached (stage 3d, C74), so
# there was nothing to protect.
genomic_to_tx <- function(gp, es, ee, s) {
  if (s == "-") { es <- rev(es); ee <- rev(ee) }
  cum <- 0L
  for (j in seq_along(es)) {
    if (s == "+" && gp >= es[j] && gp <= ee[j]) return(cum + (gp - es[j]) + 1L)
    if (s == "-" && gp >= es[j] && gp <= ee[j]) return(cum + (ee[j] - gp) + 1L)
    cum <- cum + (ee[j] - es[j] + 1L)
  }
  NA_integer_
}

bs <- structures[match(broad$comparator_isoform_id, isoform_id)]
ref_tx <- integer(nrow(broad)); td2_tx <- integer(nrow(broad))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(broad))) {
  es <- bs$exon_starts[[i]]; ee <- bs$exon_ends[[i]]
  s  <- broad$strand_use[i]
  if (length(es) == 0L || is.na(broad$ref_atg_genomic[i]) ||
      is.na(broad$td2_atg_genomic[i])) {
    ref_tx[i] <- NA_integer_; td2_tx[i] <- NA_integer_; next
  }
  ref_tx[i] <- genomic_to_tx(broad$ref_atg_genomic[i], es, ee, s)
  td2_tx[i] <- genomic_to_tx(broad$td2_atg_genomic[i], es, ee, s)
}
broad[, ref_atg_tx_pos := ref_tx]
broad[, td2_atg_tx_pos := td2_tx]
broad[, distance_nt   := td2_atg_tx_pos - ref_atg_tx_pos]
broad_clean <- broad[!is.na(ref_atg_tx_pos) & !is.na(td2_atg_tx_pos)]

# Kozak PWM scoring — load sequences for broad_clean comparators from the
# nmd_lungcells corrected FASTA via awk (avoid full Biostrings dependency).
load_sequences <- function(isoform_ids, fasta_path) {
  ids <- unique(isoform_ids)
  id_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
  writeLines(ids, id_file); on.exit(unlink(id_file), add = TRUE)
  awk_cmd <- sprintf(
    "awk 'BEGIN{while((getline id < \"%s\") > 0) want[id]=1} /^>/{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq; hdr=substr($1,2); found=(hdr in want); seq=\"\"; next} found{seq=seq$0} END{if(seq && found) print hdr \"\\t\" seq}' '%s'",
    id_file, fasta_path)
  raw <- system(awk_cmd, intern = TRUE)
  split_raw <- strsplit(raw, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
  setNames(toupper(vapply(split_raw, `[`, character(1), 2)),
                   vapply(split_raw, `[`, character(1), 1))
}
seqs <- load_sequences(broad_clean$comparator_isoform_id, FASTA_PATH)
pwm_seqs <- character(nrow(broad_clean))
for (k in seq_len(nrow(broad_clean))) {
  cid <- broad_clean$comparator_isoform_id[k]
  if (cid %in% names(seqs)) pwm_seqs[k] <- seqs[cid]
}
v_ref <- !is.na(broad_clean$ref_atg_tx_pos) & pwm_seqs != ""
v_td2 <- !is.na(broad_clean$td2_atg_tx_pos) & pwm_seqs != ""
ref_pwm <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(broad_clean)); td2_pwm <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(broad_clean))
if (sum(v_ref) > 0) {
  r <- Isopair::scoreKozakPWM(pwm_seqs[v_ref], broad_clean$ref_atg_tx_pos[v_ref])
  ref_pwm[v_ref] <- r$score
}
if (sum(v_td2) > 0) {
  r <- Isopair::scoreKozakPWM(pwm_seqs[v_td2], broad_clean$td2_atg_tx_pos[v_td2])
  td2_pwm[v_td2] <- r$score
}
broad_clean[, ref_kozak := ref_pwm]
broad_clean[, td2_kozak := td2_pwm]

# Broad-scope summary stats — ratio convention TD2/ref-AUG (matches the
# TD2BiasEvidence supplement). For PTC+ pairs TD2 picks a downstream ATG
# that extends past the PTC, so TD2 ORF > ref-AUG ORF on average.
broad_orf_ratio <- median(broad_clean$td2_orf_nt) / median(broad_clean$ref_atg_orf_nt)
broad_koz_valid  <- !is.na(broad_clean$ref_kozak) & !is.na(broad_clean$td2_kozak)
broad_n_kozak    <- sum(broad_koz_valid)
broad_n_ref_gt   <- sum(broad_clean$ref_kozak[broad_koz_valid] >
                         broad_clean$td2_kozak[broad_koz_valid])
broad_n_ref_eq   <- sum(broad_clean$ref_kozak[broad_koz_valid] ==
                         broad_clean$td2_kozak[broad_koz_valid])
broad_n_nontied  <- broad_n_kozak - broad_n_ref_eq
broad_koz_w      <- wilcox.test(broad_clean$ref_kozak[broad_koz_valid],
                                 broad_clean$td2_kozak[broad_koz_valid],
                                 paired = TRUE)
broad_pos_eq    <- sum(broad_clean$distance_nt == 0L)
broad_pos_down  <- sum(broad_clean$distance_nt > 0L)
broad_pos_up    <- sum(broad_clean$distance_nt < 0L)
broad_pos_pct_down <- 100 * broad_pos_down / nrow(broad_clean)

# Occult-PTC subset
occ <- broad_clean[category == "effectively_ptc" & original_ptc == FALSE]
occ_orf_ratio <- median(occ$td2_orf_nt) / median(occ$ref_atg_orf_nt)
occ_koz_valid <- !is.na(occ$ref_kozak) & !is.na(occ$td2_kozak)
occ_n_kozak   <- sum(occ_koz_valid)
occ_n_ref_gt  <- sum(occ$ref_kozak[occ_koz_valid] > occ$td2_kozak[occ_koz_valid])
occ_n_ref_eq  <- sum(occ$ref_kozak[occ_koz_valid] == occ$td2_kozak[occ_koz_valid])
occ_n_nontied <- occ_n_kozak - occ_n_ref_eq
occ_koz_w     <- wilcox.test(occ$ref_kozak[occ_koz_valid],
                              occ$td2_kozak[occ_koz_valid], paired = TRUE)
occ_pos_down  <- sum(occ$distance_nt > 0L)
occ_pos_pct_down <- 100 * occ_pos_down / nrow(occ)
```

## §4a — TD2 vs ref-AUG ORF length

| Scope | n | TD2 median ORF (nt) | ref-AUG median ORF (nt) | TD2/ref ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Broad | `r format(nrow(broad_clean), big.mark=",")` | `r format(median(broad_clean$td2_orf_nt), big.mark=",")` | `r format(median(broad_clean$ref_atg_orf_nt), big.mark=",")` | **`r sprintf("%.2f×", broad_orf_ratio)`** |
| Occult-PTC | `r format(nrow(occ), big.mark=",")` | `r format(median(occ$td2_orf_nt), big.mark=",")` | `r format(median(occ$ref_atg_orf_nt), big.mark=",")` | **`r sprintf("%.2f×", occ_orf_ratio)`** |

## §4b — Paired Kozak PWM at ref AUG vs TD2 ATG

The "ref > TD2 (% of all)" column counts pairs where the ref-AUG Kozak score
exceeds TD2's — pooled over all pairs including ties (broad scope has many
pairs where TD2 == ref AUG, distance 0). The "% of non-tied" column drops
ties so the directional preference is unobscured. The paired-Wilcoxon p-value
is computed on the raw score vector, ignoring ties as `wilcox.test` does.

| Scope | n | ref > TD2 | ties | ref > TD2 (% of all) | ref > TD2 (% of non-tied) | Paired-Wilcoxon p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Broad | `r format(broad_n_kozak, big.mark=",")` | `r format(broad_n_ref_gt, big.mark=",")` | `r format(broad_n_ref_eq, big.mark=",")` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * broad_n_ref_gt / broad_n_kozak)` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * broad_n_ref_gt / broad_n_nontied)` | `r format_p(broad_koz_w$p.value)` |
| Occult-PTC | `r format(occ_n_kozak, big.mark=",")` | `r format(occ_n_ref_gt, big.mark=",")` | `r format(occ_n_ref_eq, big.mark=",")` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * occ_n_ref_gt / occ_n_kozak)` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * occ_n_ref_gt / occ_n_nontied)` | `r format_p(occ_koz_w$p.value)` |

## §4c — TD2 ATG position relative to ref AUG

| Scope | n | TD2 == ref | TD2 downstream | TD2 upstream | % downstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Broad | `r format(nrow(broad_clean), big.mark=",")` | `r format(broad_pos_eq, big.mark=",")` | `r format(broad_pos_down, big.mark=",")` | `r format(broad_pos_up, big.mark=",")` | **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", broad_pos_pct_down)`** |
| Occult-PTC | `r format(nrow(occ), big.mark=",")` | `r format(sum(occ$distance_nt == 0L), big.mark=",")` | `r format(occ_pos_down, big.mark=",")` | `r format(sum(occ$distance_nt < 0L), big.mark=",")` | **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", occ_pos_pct_down)`** |

In the occult-PTC scope, **TD2 selects an ATG downstream of the ref-AUG in
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", occ_pos_pct_down)` of pairs**, with a Kozak score lower
than the ref-AUG in `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * occ_n_ref_gt / occ_n_kozak)`
of pairs (paired-Wilcoxon `r format_p(occ_koz_w$p.value)`). The TD2 ORF is
`r sprintf("%.2f×", occ_orf_ratio)` LONGER than the ref-AUG-projected ORF
(ratio of medians) — TD2 picks a downstream ATG that extends past the PTC into an
in-frame coding region, producing a longer ORF that lacks the EJC-downstream
stop that defines a PTC. Together these three signals describe TD2's
PTC-avoidance bias: TD2 systematically routes around occult PTCs by picking a
downstream ATG, even at the cost of a lower Kozak score.

```{r sec4-supp, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="TD2BiasEvidence supplement — 2×3 layout: broad scope (row 1, n=819) + occult-PTC scope (row 2, n=348)", out.width="100%"}
inc_fig(
  c(file.path(FIG_ROOT, "figures/supplemental/SF34_TD2Bias_broad/figure_sf34.png"),
    file.path(FIG_ROOT, "figures/supplemental/SF35_TD2Bias_occult/figure_sf35.png"))
)
```

# §5 — Cumulative accounting [verification chokepoint]

Recompute from §2 / §3 result objects so the totals in this report can be
audited end-to-end without trusting upstream caches.

```{r sec5-accounting, include=FALSE}
secA_ptc_pos  <- length(ptc_pos_ids)
secA_ptc_neg  <- length(ptc_neg_ids)
secA_total    <- nrow(gencode_all3_c2)
stopifnot(
  "§2a NMD denominator drift"   = n_avail_nmd  == secA_total,
  "§2a Control denominator drift" = n_avail_ctrl == nrow(gencode_all3_c4),
  "§2a PTC+ + PTC- != Section A total" = secA_ptc_pos + secA_ptc_neg == secA_total,
  "§2b mechanism table sum != unique direct attributions" =
    sum(mech_tab$n) == n_unique_direct
)

get_n <- function(df, g) {
  v <- df$n[df$group == g]
  if (length(v) == 0L) 0L else v
}
secC_ptc_pos  <- get_n(sec3_class, "NMD+/PTC+")
secC_ptc_neg  <- get_n(sec3_class, "NMD+/PTC-")
secC_ref_abs  <- get_n(sec3_class, "Ref AUG absent")
secC_total    <- nrow(refaug_matched_c2)
stopifnot(
  "§3 class sum != Section C total" =
    secC_ptc_pos + secC_ptc_neg + secC_ref_abs == secC_total,
  "§3a Control denominator != Section C total" =
    length(sec_C_groups$Control) == secC_total
)

acct <- data.frame(
  Scope = c("Section A (n=130)", "Section C (n=819)"),
  PTC_pos = c(secA_ptc_pos, secC_ptc_pos),
  PTC_neg = c(secA_ptc_neg, secC_ptc_neg),
  Ref_AUG_absent = c(NA_integer_, secC_ref_abs),
  Total = c(secA_total, secC_total),
  PTC_pos_rate_pct = c(round(100 * secA_ptc_pos / secA_total, 1),
                       round(100 * secC_ptc_pos / secC_total, 1))
)
```

```{r sec5-acct-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(acct,
             caption = "Cumulative accounting at both canonical scopes",
             col.names = c("Scope", "PTC+", "PTC−", "Ref AUG absent",
                           "Total", "PTC+ rate (%)"))
```

- **Section A (n=`r secA_total`):** `r secA_ptc_pos` PTC+ and `r secA_ptc_neg` PTC− sum to `r secA_total`. PTC+ rate **`r round(100 * secA_ptc_pos / secA_total, 1)`%**.
- **Section C (n=`r format(secC_total, big.mark=",")`):** `r format(secC_ptc_pos, big.mark=",")` PTC+, `r secC_ptc_neg` PTC−, and `r secC_ref_abs` Ref-AUG-absent sum to `r format(secC_total, big.mark=",")`. PTC+ rate **`r round(100 * secC_ptc_pos / secC_total, 1)`%**.

**Why the two scopes give different PTC+ rates** is a methodological — not
biological — divergence:

| Difference | Section A | Section C |
|---|---|---|
| Cohort filter | all-3-ENST + coding-CDS (most stringent) | ENST-reference only (broader) |
| PTC classifier | own-GENCODE-stop + 50-nt rule | ref-AUG-projected `category == "effectively_ptc"` |
| Comparator CDS source | curated GENCODE | TD2 (heavily debiased via ref-AUG projection) |
| Selection-on-PTC | none — every coding-CDS comparator measured | TR-category filter requires ref-AUG-traceable ORF — pairs where ref-AUG points at "no_downstream_ejc" or "truncated_no_ejc" classify as PTC− regardless of comparator's own stop |

The Section C 90% PTC+ rate is enriched by the TR-category filter, which
removes pairs where ref-AUG tracing finds no PTC and no stop near the EJC.
The Section A 38% PTC+ rate has no such pre-filter: it's the raw PTC rate
across all GENCODE-only NMD pairs. The two rates are not directly
comparable. The point of measuring both is to show that the §2-§4 5'UTR /
ORF / Kozak signals replicate at both scopes.

# §6 — What is intentionally NOT in this Rmd

These analyses remain in `05_final_report_mashr.Rmd` (legacy-bannered) or
`06_orf_analysis_mashr.Rmd` (legacy-bannered) — they are retained for
reproducibility of the prior submission and for sensitivity analyses:

- Reclassification two-pass (TD2 → ref-AUG handoff at the old scope) — legacy
  `05_final_report_mashr.Rmd`.
- Per-cell-type PTC stratification at the old scope — legacy
  `05_final_report_mashr.Rmd`.
- "85% combined" framework — legacy `05_final_report_mashr.Rmd`.
- n=1,904 / n=22,335 GENCODE-only 3'UTR outside-set — legacy
  `05_final_report_mashr.Rmd`.
- ORF / deep-learning model analyses — `06_orf_analysis_mashr.Rmd` (in this
  repo, legacy). The canonical home of the manuscript deep-learning model is
  the **linked repo `peter4244/NMD_orf_model_v5_4ct`**: `03_train.py`,
  `config.yaml`, `model.py`, `METHODS.md`, plus DeepSHAP / KernelSHAP scripts.
  The "ORF identification is the bottleneck" headline result lives there.

Cross-cell-type consistency checks are out of scope for this Rmd; per-CT
mashr CSVs in `shortread_dge/mashr/` and `isocall_dge/mashr/` are the source
of truth for CT-stratified numbers.
